Subject: Re: Inquiry: blended SKU pricing for hybrid deployment + partner split

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Putting an initial sketch together below and attaching a pricing matrix and a short term sheet (see attachments). High-level answers first, details after.

Short answers:
- Blended SKU approach: we can offer a "SKU Fusion" that sets a committed annual minimum (units = token-hours equivalent) with three volume tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold). List price is the public marketplace list price; private-offer discounts apply against list price. Overage billing is hourly at a defined capped rate if you exceed committed capacity.
- Partner margin: we support two patterns: (A) partner pass-through where reseller takes a fixed % of list price invoiced separately (preferred for tax clarity), or (B) carve-out where the reseller uplift is taken from Redwood's net (we can do a blended split to preserve the customer's unit economics). We recommend pass-through for EMEA to keep VAT flows clean.

Attached: nexon-pricing-matrix-v1.xlsx (matrix with example volumes & blended rates), sku-fusion-term-sheet.pdf (term summary).

Detailed notes:
- Pricing mechanics: list price L, committed discount Dc per band, partner pass-through P% applied to L (invoiced by partner). Effective customer net = L * (1 - Dc) + overage.
- Overage cadence: hourly metering with daily aggregation; tiered cap for peak burst (you can pre-book burst capacity at negotiated rate to avoid overage).
- Tax: for EU-hosted private control plane we recommend partner invoicing to handle VAT where applicable — we'll provide template invoices and VAT evidence.

Next steps:
1) Camila will produce a pro forma showing the two partner split options (pass-through vs carve-out) and the impact on Nexon's P&L.
2) Olga will review contract language for reseller carve-out and tax clauses.
3) Diego to schedule a 45-min procurement + channel call before your Thursday review.

Would Thursday 09/10 10:00 CEST work for a joint call?

Best,
Diego

Circling back with a few legal notes for the draft term-sheet (short list):

- Reseller pass-through: good for VAT handling. If partner invoices the customer, ensure the distribution agreement includes a "tax representation" clause so partner is responsible for invoicing and VAT reporting.
- Carve-out model: we need clear language on calculation of the reseller uplift and gross-to-net reconciliation timing (quarterly true-up recommended). Otherwise finance disputes surface.
- Data residency & audit: if the private nodes are in EU zones, add an SLA appendix that confirms audit log retention and KMS key provenance. Procurement will want this on the procurement artifact.

I'll put minor redlines into sku-fusion-term-sheet.pdf and return by EOD tomorrow.

—Olga

Redwood Inference
